answer_1.quote: Privacy-Conscious Delegation requires trusted, weaker models to use untrusted, powerful models as tools to fulfill private user requests ... the system's goal is to produce an output response r of the best possible quality, using one or both LLMs, while revealing as little private information as possible to the untrusted LLM.
answer_1.outputs: Generated responses to user queries (final output r) after possible delegation to remote LLM

answer_2.quote: We define metrics for Privacy-Conscious Delegation, measuring (i) how well systems preserve response quality in comparison to using the best-in-class API models and (ii) how much private information systems leak to the API model.
automatic_metrics: Privacy Leakage (percentage of PII units present in prompt)
Cosine Similarity between final output and proprietary model response

answer_3.quote: We employ LLMs as a judge for these two qualities. We query the LLM judge to directly determine whether the quality of the output ... and we also use an LLM judge to assess privacy leakage in the synthesized prompt.
methods: pairwise quality judgment (response A vs. response B)
privacy leakage judgment (presence of PII in prompt)

answer_4.quote: We conduct a human evaluation for our QUAL(A, B) metric on Prolific ... participants are asked to select the better response from the two candidates or mark the two as tied in quality. ... we evaluated how well our privacy leakage metric aligns with human judgment ... participants indicated whether they agree with the privacy leakage score.
answer_4.guideline: For quality: participants choose which of two responses is better or mark them as tied. For privacy leakage: participants are given the PII units and the synthesized prompt and indicate whether the prompt leaks any private information.
